subject: Civil Engineering
title: Base Isolation: Floating on Bearings
description: A 60-second lesson on Base Isolation: Floating on Bearings.

hook.text: What if the building didn't feel the earthquake at all? Base isolation makes that possible.

buildup.text: Rubber bearings between the foundation and the building let the ground move underneath.

discovery.text: Lead-rubber bearings flex slowly during quakes — absorbing energy while centering the building.

twist.text: The building barely sways while the ground beneath moves inches — occupants feel almost nothing.

climax.text: Japan's base-isolated hospitals continued operating during the 2011 earthquake — fully functional.

punchline.text: Disconnect the building from the ground and the earthquake passes beneath it.

quiz.question: How do base isolation bearings protect a building?
options: They strengthen the foundation to resist earthquake forces directly
They allow the ground to move beneath the building while the structure stays relatively still
They absorb sound waves from the earthquake to reduce shaking
